newsitem.title: UK: UK's Powergen looking at Germany's Bewag-FT.
newsitem.headline: UK's Powergen looking at Germany's Bewag-FT.

text.p: British electricity generator Powergen Plc is mulling making an offer for Germany's Berlin Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag), the utility which supplies Berlin with electricity, the Financial Times said on Wednesday. The FT quoted Peter Hughes, director of Powergen's international operations, as saying the deal was at a very early stage as it "was not clear what was being offered".
Bewag will be privatised early next year.

On December 16, Bewag chief executive Dietmar Winje told shareholders that after the sale of Berlin's shareholding, the company expects any future investors to strengthen the company economically and improve its competitiveness.
Currently 50.8 percent of Bewag is owned by Berlin, with 10 percent held by Viag AG unit Bayernwerk and Veba AG's PreussenElektra, respectively.
The remaining shares are spread among smaller shareholders.
